TASK-1945 S3a, C1 (one commit-keyed CI reader). `gh pr list --search STORY-1689` finds no PR, so S3a is landing the shared reader. Please pass this to lane impl-story-1689 so it builds on it instead of writing a second one.

Where: aida-cli-lib/src/forge_commit_ci.rs, a submodule of forge.rs re-exported as crate::forge::*.
- github_commit_checks(repo "owner/name", sha, api) and gitlab_commit_checks(project, sha, api). `api` is a FnMut(&str endpoint) -> Result<Vec<u8>> that runs `gh api` / `glab api`, so each caller keeps its own host pinning and timeout.
- GitHub: commits/{sha}/check-runs, paginated (up to 10 pages, refused if the listing falls short of total_count), plus commits/{sha}/status. GitLab: repository/commits/{sha}/statuses, keeping the newest job per name.
- Every check must be on that SHA. Any CLI, API or parse failure is Err; nothing degrades to None.
- judge_commit_checks(&checks, required) -> CommitCi { Green, NoChecks, MissingRequired(name), Pending(names), Failed(names) }. Success/neutral/skipped pass; an allowed GitLab failure passes.
- For STORY-1689, the CiTarget::Commit fix becomes a thin call: GitHubForge::ci_status(Commit) runs github_commit_checks through self.gh and maps CommitCi to CiStatus. Map Err, NoChecks and MissingRequired to ci-unknown.

One point needs your ruling. The check-runs API has no check named "Build / Require every CI lane". The aggregator's check run is the job "Build (ubuntu-latest)" (ci.yml build-result); "Require every CI lane" is its only step. I require CI_AGGREGATOR_CHECK = "Build (ubuntu-latest)". This is a const, so in a non-AIDA repo `aida review watch` always reports "not ready: CI check `Build (ubuntu-latest)` has not reported". If that matters, a follow-up could make it configurable. PR number and head to follow.
subject: TASK-1945 S3a: shared commit-keyed CI reader (C1)
